A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RefineStat study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite reference reflow and changed appendix pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original program-generation experiments, Bayesian diagnostic and ELPD results, component ablations, and appendix analyses of token efficiency and memorization.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices, including the PyMC and NumPyro evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same semantic validation, prior/likelihood resampling, diagnostic acceptance criteria, and ELPD-based selection. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Eight Schools, Dugongs, Surgical, Peregrine, and Poisson GP data. The PyMC/NumPyro evaluations and anonymized/obfuscated prompt scenarios are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including Standard/SynCode in Table 1, Expert/BoxLM/OpenAI o3 in Table 3, and IterGen/refinement variants in Table 8. The newly cited debugging methods are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–E retain the same prompts, model configurations, temperature settings, posterior-sampling instructions, diagnostic thresholds, and baseline-selection procedures.

E4.justification: The validation ablation in Table 4, structural examples in Appendix C, error analysis in Appendix F, and token-efficiency and memorization studies in Appendix G are unchanged.

E5.justification: The five-repeat description in Section 5.2, ten-seed statements in the ablation/setup passages, and mean/standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds uncertainty estimates or revises run-count information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and their accompanying findings retain the same entries and numerical values. Examples include RefineStat's 0.45/0.50/0.50 run rates in Table 1 and the 1.9x average token ratio in Table 8.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–10, semantic predicates, reliability-score construction, model-selection objective, and appendix equations are unchanged. The added punctuation in Definition 2 does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reliable probabilistic synthesis using small language models, semantic constraints, and diagnostic refinement. The added code-access sentence does not change a scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and failure explanations remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations concerning omitted prior/posterior predictive checks, incomplete assessment of model adequacy, and lack of a global-optimum guarantee.

D1.justification: v2 Section 9 describes supplementary source code and promises an open-source release. v3 removes that section and supplies a specific code-repository address in the abstract. Prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and other appendix implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a short connection to probabilistic-program debugging, citing Dutta et al. (2019, 2022) and Nussbaumer et al. (2026) as potential sources of synthesis feedback. SynCode and IterGen reference consolidation retains the same underlying works.

P1.justification: Localized edits add code-access and related-work sentences, remove the separate reproducibility statement, update the conference header, and streamline citations and bibliographic metadata. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the reproducibility statement and shortening bibliographic entries reflows the reference pages; Definition 2 also receives a small spacing adjustment. Figures 1–2, Algorithm 1, and Tables 1–9 retain their visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: The concrete repository address improves code-access guidance over v2's supplementary-code and future-release statement, while the debugging citations modestly improve research context. Removing the standalone statement does not remove the detailed technical appendices. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
